text:
maria: Quick sync — last deploy caused a big autoscaler churn because our deploy-time warmers fired all at once. I want to try a staggered prefill + "traffic blender" approach so we avoid synchronized bursts. Thoughts?

ajay: +1 — we saw KV cache thrash too. If every warmer uses the same prefix keys at T0 we get eviction and kernel cold paths.

kelly: Agree. Can we do per-deployer jitter + route-aware keying? e.g., group routes by model/seq-len and spread warmers across a 10–30m window.

samir: Also: mix synthetic short prompts with a few longer, real-ish prefix shapes to prime attention/kvcaches. Short only is cheaper but misses KV access patterns for longer inferences.

maria: Exactly. Proposal sketch:
- Deploy-time warmers run in waves: 0%, 10%, 30%, 60%, 100% allocation over a configurable window (default 20m).
- Each wave picks keys using a route-aware sampler: top N recent prefixes + synthetic blended templates.
- Add small random jitter per-worker (0–90s) to avoid micro-sync.

ajay: For keying: use (route_id, model_family, prefix_fingerprint) instead of raw text. That keeps cardinality sane and stable across minor prompt tweaks.

kelly: We should also respect autoscaler signals: if GPUs are at 95% util, pause further waves and backoff. No point thrashing an overloaded pool.

samir: What about kernel selection and batching? If we prefill with a lot of small requests we could bias the runtime to choose small-batch kernels and then suffer on real large-batch traffic. Need to include mix of batch sizes in the synthetic traffic.

maria: Good catch. Include a distribution of sequence lengths and target batch sizes in the blend. Default distribution: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% med (64–512), 10% long (512+). Also randomize inter-request spacing so batching heuristics remain realistic.

maria: Example prefill job config (draft):
```yaml
job_name: deploy-prefill-wave
window_minutes: 20
waves: [0, 10, 30, 60, 100]
sampler:
  recent_prefixes: 50
  synthetic_templates: 100
  prefix_keying: route:model_family:prefix_hash
blend:
  short_ratio: 0.6
  med_ratio: 0.3
  long_ratio: 0.1
jitter_seconds: 90
backoff_on_util_pct: 95
metrics_to_emit: [prefill.hitrate, prefill.cost, prefill.latency_p50, gpu.util]
```

david: I can add a lightweight prefill scheduler in the deploy pipeline that writes a prefill plan to S3 and the runtime picks up the plan during rollout. That isolates deploy-plane logic and lets us vary per-customer policies.

kelly: For observability, add these dashboards/alerts:
- prefill.hitrate by route (aim > 60% after wave 3)
- prefill.evictions (should be near 0)
- kernel.switches per minute (spike indicates biasing)
- on-demand cold starts per route (should drop)

ajay: We'll want an experiment flag so we can A/B the staggered warmers vs. baseline on a small fraction of deploys. Keep the default off for now.

maria: Agreed. Rollout plan: canary 1% (2 deployments) -> 10% -> 50% -> all, with automatic abort if prefill.hitrate < 30% after second wave or gpu.util spikes > 90% sustained for 5m.

samir: Minor perf regression risk: synthetic prompts might PATH through different attention kernels if we don't mimic positional distributions correctly. Make sure some templates include longer prefix tokens at non-zero positions.

maria: Good note. I'll add a template set that includes early-offset tokens, repeated tokens, and long-context tokens.

runtime-bot: prefill-job scheduled: deploy-prefill-wave (canary) for deploy/2026-03-17T15:12Z — plan_id=pf-20260317-01

deploy-bot: kickoff logs: wave0 started (0% allocation) — 12 workers assigned, sampler seeded from recent prefixes.

runtime-bot: log: wave1 (10%) started after jitter; emitted 2.4k synthetic requests, observed prefill.hitrate=18% (route=chat-stream), prefill.evictions=3, gpu.util=47%

maria: Early numbers look fine, evictions are low. Hitrate is low for chat-stream but that's expected for wave1. Keep monitoring.

ajay: Idea: add a short-lived KV pin for high-value keys during prefill (TTL 30m) to prevent immediate eviction while traffic ramps. Pinning should be conservative.

kelly: Agree but add a safety cap: max pinned keys per-worker = 100. Also emit pinned.key_count.

david: I'll instrument the runtime to expose kernel selection distribution (small-batch vs large-batch kernels) so we can verify we're not biasing.

samir: Once canary finishes, capture a 15m profile (kernels, batching histogram, kv.hit_by_prefix) and compare to baseline to detect regressions early.

maria: Thanks all — action items:
- david: add prefill plan pickup in deploy pipeline + S3 write
- samir/ajay: add sampler/keying logic + pinning guard
- kelly: dashboards/alerts + experiment flag controls
- maria: prepare template set and rollout criteria

maria: We'll reconvene after canary end (ETA ~40m). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
